searchText: My question: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1570846883927167077/1570858689919721583 Honestly no one seriously considers 50/25 Mbit requirements. Increasing bandwidth requirements gives more confidence we can propagate signatures in 2-3 seconds and finish the whole aggregation pipeline before next slot Even if we the network is heterogenous? I'd imagine that people would say 20% of nodes are 50/25 then 40% is gigabit or something like this I'm assuming you mean this even with bls simulations? Maybe its just me in some bubble, but I never heard of someone actually running their validators on 50/25 connection. Every home staker I asked had at least 100Mbit connection (usually more). I think % of 50/25 nodes is actually very low or 0 okay, I just rechecked Sukun's BLS 8334 [simulations](https://github.com/ethereum/dc-networking/blob/main/personal/sukun/eip-8334.html) . Indeed he was assuming 50/25 nodes just saying, eip 7870 is exactly 21 months old:) Ah right, I agree that many validators will not be on 50/25 😄 Yeah I would be interested in what it gets us tbh, and I think its reasonable to say that only X% of the network is running 50/25 yeah, we can compare 50/25 with 100/50 Do we know today how many attesters are running on 50/25? Just to get an idea and see if this is an absolute minority. Not sure, though I personally would be more cautious when raising bandwidth numbers as opposed to compute 😄 that can give a good idea of the likely smallest nodes we have on the network https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1569690422010191873/1570816644811460638 that said I'm not convinced we can make any kind of conclusion regarding raising requirements until we know what the network needs to support in the first place. e.g, we could be having 2x larger signatures if we need to support DVT. doesn't seem to me that we quite have the right models and simulations to make the decision, and I'd tread carefully with anything that raises the entry of validators on the network. as you know I believe there are good reasons to do so more generally speaking, but these are still delicate questions where the burden of proof is on increasing requirements I agree
